(1) Both models tie at quality 0.92. Python `sorted` is stable, so equal-key order keeps `results` order. `run_bench` appends from a thread pool as each call returns, so `results` order is whichever model finishes first — a completion race. `ranked[0]` is that race winner, not a defined quality champion.

(2) Locally/in isolation, low scheduler noise often keeps completion order stable (claude-opus tends to finish first). CI load/jitter reorders completions ~1/5. Solo re-runs rarely recreate that interleaving.

(3) Fix: deterministic secondary key, e.g. `sorted(results, key=lambda r: (-r['quality'], r['model']))`, or assert max quality / membership among tops — not a single model name under ties.

Test bug, not product bug (unless a documented product tie-break is missing in `run_bench`).
